# Stage 4: Metric library

Define each number goals are measured by once (its meaning and calculation, unit, direction, source and owner), and say which metric measures a goal, for a team or the whole company. The [Metric library module](../modules/metrics/README.md), from its `module.json`.

**Today:** an outline: entry and exit criteria, checked by hand, with no drill yet.

## Entry criteria

- Stages 1 to 3 pass their exit criteria.
- The core keeps a module’s own records (stage 2): a save carries them with the core’s, in one transaction; the workspace holds them by module and record; a removal saves them as changed, and Undo puts each back as it was just before.
- Goals have a unit (metric and range goals) and teams have ids, so a link can check its unit and slice.

## What to build

The metric library, and the worked example of a module with records of its own. A metric (name, meaning and calculation, unit, decimals, which way is better, source and its owner, refresh, owner, caveats) is defined once per workspace, and a goal links to one metric for a slice (a team, or the whole company), the goal’s own target being the target in it. Anyone adds a metric; its owner or an admin changes or removes it; the goal’s owner or an admin links and unlinks. Every change is logged, removing and unlinking keep the row and come back with Undo or Recently removed, and the AI tools do the same under the same rules. Its two records are its own, not the core’s: the module declares each (what one row is, its table, where a save and the workspace file it, whether it can be removed) with its rows each way, what a new cycle carries over (every metric not removed; the links in force to the cycle’s live goals) and how a removed metric comes back, and the core’s store, removal, restore, cycle and export keep them without knowing what they are. Its rules sit in its own folder, as pure as the core’s. Its own place, /metrics: the library (find by name, unit, owner or meaning; filter by unit, the team or the whole company a goal measures it for, owner, direction, unused, or something to sort out; sort A to Z, by most goals or by the latest change; 50 a page), a page per metric with its meaning, every goal measured by it side by side (status, slice, now, target, against plan) and what it still needs, an item in the menu after People, and the metric on a goal’s page and on a person’s and a team’s. “Measured by” in the goal forms: find a metric by typing (or add one there); choosing it on a new goal fills in its unit, decimals and direction; Goals filters by the metric. Defining one well: three things to be usable, the rest said later and named in words (“Fully defined” or “Still to say: …”, never a score), and three questions answered once before saving (a close name, a unit spelt another way, a percentage that doesn’t say out of what), with each Must fix and Check under its field. Looking after one: what it still needs, a confirm before changing a unit or direction goals use, and on Workspace → About how many metrics have no owner.

What it adds to the core (routes, places on core screens, AI tools, Help) is in [its section](../modules/metrics/README.md#what-it-adds-to-the-core).

It keeps records of its own, which the core stores without knowing what they are: metric (`okr_metrics`), metric link (`okr_goal_metrics`). Every field is in [its records](../modules/metrics/records.md); how the core keeps a module’s records is stage 2’s (`src/domain/records.ts`): declared rows each way, what a new cycle carries, and how a removed one comes back, saved with the core’s in one transaction.

## Exit criteria

1. Its requirements hold: `METRICS-LIBRARY`, `METRICS-MEASURED-BY`, `METRICS-CARE`, `METRIC-DEFINED` (words in [its section](../modules/metrics/README.md#requirements)).
2. Its journeys and checks can be done: U81, U82, U83, U145, U105, F15, N16 ([its section](../modules/metrics/README.md#journeys-and-checks)).
3. A metric with a name, a unit and a direction saves; without any one of them it is refused with what is missing, and a second metric with the same name (any case) is refused.
4. Only a metric’s owner or an admin can change or remove it; only a goal’s owner or an admin can link or unlink the goal.
5. A goal in hours can’t be measured by a metric in minutes, and a goal with dated stages can’t be measured at all; a goal aiming the other way from the metric’s better direction links, with a warning.
6. Removing a metric unlinks every goal it measured in the same save; Undo straight after brings the metric and the links back; restoring it later brings the metric back with the links it had to goals still there.
7. The demo workspace’s 13 metrics and 12 links load, and every goal’s numbers, status and dates are exactly as without them (the conformance rows don’t move).
8. Built without the module, a workspace that holds its rows loads and saves, and none of its rows is changed or deleted; with the module back, they are all there.
9. The library finds what each of rule 1’s worked examples says, a metric’s goals are rule 2’s rows in its order, and what a metric needs is rule 3’s, in order: every row of spec/conformance/metrics.csv matches.
10. The library is in the menu after People (under More on a phone); the old addresses of Metrics under Data lead to the library, a metric or the form; a metric’s row in the library counts the same goals by status as its page’s table lists (journey U81, checks F15 and N16).
11. In New goal, “Measured by” comes first on the measure step: a metric found by typing shows its meaning, fills in the unit, decimals and which way is better on a goal nobody typed them for, measures it for the goal’s team or the whole company, and Check says so; one added there is chosen; a goal with dated stages has none (journey U82, rule 5’s worked examples).
12. Adding a metric with a name close to one in use asks about it and still saves (rule 4’s worked examples); changing a unit or direction goals use asks first; Remove names the goals it stops measuring and Undo brings them back; admins see on Workspace → About how many metrics have no owner (journey U83).
13. Adding a metric needs only a name, a unit and which way is better; its page then says what is still to say in words (“Fully defined”, or “Still to say: …”, and “Its owner has left.”), never a number, and every metric in the demo says the line rule 6 gives (the conformance rows `still`). A name a letter or a word from another’s or one a metric used to have, a unit spelt another way, and a percentage that doesn’t say out of what are each a Check answered once before saving, on the form and through save_metric’s checks and answers (rule 6’s worked examples; journey U105).

## Gaps in the kit

- Owner-only rights and other governance, versions and draft states are left out on purpose (growth.md).
- The goals table is where slices side by side and numbers read from the source would grow (growth.md: dimensions an admin defines; numbers from the source).
- Left out on purpose and written down as ways to grow: spec/modules/metrics/growth.md.
